subject: ISV partnership: retainer + lead siloing and tiered commission
messages:
From: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@lumenisv.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: retainer + tiered revenue-share + lead registration

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the LumenISV team left excited about the potential integrations. Before we push to legal, we wanted to give a concise commercial framework to see if we can get alignment on three items: a small monthly retainer for marketplace integration/enablement, a tiered revenue-share on referrals/resales, and a simple lead-registration mechanism (we want to avoid double-crediting across our channel).

High-level asks from our side:
- Retainer: $6k / month for the first 6 months of the integration (covers engineering prioritization and co-marketing).
- Rev-share: 10% of Redwood net revenue for direct referrals up to $250k ARR, 8% for the next $250k, then 5% beyond.
- Lead registration: 12-month protection for registered leads; simple form + HubSpot-based validation.

I've attached a short retainer template and a sample lead-registration spreadsheet so your ops/legal teams can see the mechanics.

Can you confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with a 12-month protection window and how you typically handle tiered waterfalls and clawbacks for refunds/credits?

Best,
Sophie
VP Partnerships
LumenISV, Inc.
Attachment: LumenISV_Retainer_Template.pdf
Attachment: LeadRegistration_SLA.xlsx

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@lumenisv.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: retainer + tiered revenue-share + lead registration

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Short answers up front: retainer is OK to consider, tiered rev-share is workable but we'd like to tweak waterfall triggers and clawback language, and 12-month lead protection is within reason if we can scope the registration criteria tightly. 

A few clarifying questions from our side:
- Is the retainer refundable against early MRR once first paid customer closes? (we usually convert retainers into marketing/enablement credits against the first 6 months of shared GTM activity)
- For the revenue-share tiers, are those based on deal principal (gross) or Redwood net recognized revenue (post discounts and credits)?
- For lead registration, we need a minimal validation checklist (company domain, contact verification, date-stamped registration via HubSpot, and a rep-level attestation). If that is acceptable, our ops team can automate validation.

I'll loop Marissa and Ben here — Marissa will help map the lead registration flow to our partner portal, Ben will cover the finance/payout mechanics and clawback triggers. If you can confirm the two points above, we can draft a short commercial addendum for legal to review.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@lumenisv.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 12:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: retainer + tiered revenue-share + lead registration

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 11:02 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Short answers up front: retainer is OK to consider, tiered rev-share is workable but we'd like to tweak waterfall triggers and clawback language, and 12-month lead protection is within reason if we can scope the registration criteria tightly.
> 
> A few clarifying questions from our side:
> - Is the retainer refundable against early MRR once first paid customer closes? (we usually convert retainers into marketing/enablement credits against the first 6 months of shared GTM activity)
> - For the revenue-share tiers, are those based on deal principal (gross) or Redwood net recognized revenue (post discounts and credits)?
> - For lead registration, we need a minimal validation checklist (company domain, contact verification, date-stamped registration via HubSpot, and a rep-level attestation). If that is acceptable, our ops team can automate validation.

Thanks Mateo — quick responses inline: 
- Retainer: LumenISV is fine with converting the retainer into marketing credits but we prefer a partial refund if the deal doesn't move to a paid status within 9 months. Could we do a split: convert 50% to credits, refund 50% if no paid customer in 9 months?
- Rev-share basis: we'd like it to be gross ARR (before discounts) because many of our buyers buy through bundled offers where list price is meaningful for our marketplace economics.
- Registration checklist: yes to the HubSpot + attestation flow. We can add our intake form fields if that helps.

If you can confirm the 50/50 retainer conversion + 9-month refund window and whether you can accommodate gross ARR basis for the rev-share tiers, we'll push to legal.

— Sophie

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@lumenisv.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: retainer + tiered revenue-share + lead registration

Hi Sophie — looping in Partner Ops and Finance notes. We like the simplicity of Lumen's ask; couple of operational constraints from our side: 

1) Rev-share accounting: Redwood reports partner payouts based on recognized net revenue on our invoices because we need to align to ASC guidance and credits/returns. We can model a gross-to-net reconciliation to show LumenISV the expected payments, but payouts must be reconciled to net recognized revenue. If Lumen wants gross-based economics, we would need to treat the difference as a marketing adjustment (one-time uplift) rather than perpetual gross-based payouts.

2) Retainer treatment: 50/50 split (convert half to marketing credit, refund half after 9 months if no paid customer) is workable but requires an invoice credit memo flow — Ben, can you confirm how quickly finance can process the refund if the 9-month clause triggers?

3) Lead registration: the HubSpot attestation + domain/contact verification is fine. We will add a short SLA: Redwood has 5 business days to validate registrations; conflicts go to a single-arbiter escalation (Partner Ops).

Action items:
- Ben: confirm refund processing timeline and clawback mechanics (Ben, see the attached LeadRegistration_SLA.xlsx for the fields we need automated).
- Mateo + Sophie: confirm final commercial terms (we should get a single-paragraph addendum that both parties sign).
- Marissa: I will draft the registration flows and the 5-business-day SLA for validation.

Thanks — Marissa
Partner Ops | Redwood Inference
Attachment: LeadRegistration_SLA.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Sophie Lemaire <sophie@lumenisv.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: retainer + tiered revenue-share + lead registration

Marissa / Mateo — quick finance confirmation:
- Refund processing: if the 9-month refund clause triggers, we'll process a refund within 30 days of the trigger date. Refunds will be issued to the original payment method unless otherwise requested.
- Clawback mechanics: partner payouts are reconciled quarterly against net recognized revenue. If a refund/credit occurs on a customer account that affects previously paid partner commissions, we will recover overpayments via credit on the next quarterly payout cycle (standard clawback). We will provide LumenISV with a quarterly statement and an itemized reconciliation on request.

Sophie — from an operational perspective, we recommend the addendum specify that rev-share calculations are reconciled to Redwood net revenue and include an illustrative example (we can add one). If you want gross-based stable payments, we can include a one-time uplift payment to bridge the delta, but it would be a different commercial structure.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lemaire <sophie@lumenisv.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 16:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: retainer + tiered revenue-share + lead registration

Thanks everyone — Sophie, looks like we have a path to agreement. To summarize the commercial posture we'll send to legal as a one-page addendum: 
- Retainer: $6k/month for 6 months. 50% converts to co-marketing credits; the remaining 50% refundable if no paid customer closes within 9 months (refund processed within 30 days of trigger).
- Rev-share: tiered percentages as proposed, reconciled to Redwood net recognized revenue with quarterly payout and clawback on returns/credits. Redwood will provide an illustrative example in the addendum and a quarterly statement to LumenISV.
- Lead registration: 12-month protection, registration via HubSpot intake form, Redwood has 5 business days to validate, conflicts escalated to Partner Ops arbitration.

Next steps: Marissa — please draft the 1-page commercial addendum and the lead-registration SLA using the attached spreadsheet fields. Ben — we'll need that illustrative example and a note on the payout schedule for legal. Sophie — once we have the draft, I can route to our legal counsel and push the DocuSign link.

I'll also create the HubSpot deal (HS-987654) and share a DocuSign stub for signatures: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/987654 and https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-lumenisv

Thanks,
Mateo
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference
